about: Curated scholar catalogue: life years, faith label, field, main working location, concise contribution, selected works, and verified site use or holdings. Archaeology profiles and bibliographies expanded against institutional and publisher sources in October 2026; see scholars-archaeology-sources.md. `match` counts mentions in the site's own content.

scholars.name: Flavius Josephus
scholars.line: Jewish priest and soldier turned historian; his books are the fullest record of the Jewish world in the time of Jesus and the apostles.
works: The Jewish War
Antiquities of the Jews
site: His four works are in the library (Whiston's translation), planned for history notes.

scholars.name: Tacitus
scholars.line: Roman senator and historian whose Annals mention Christ's execution under Pontius Pilate.
works: Annals

scholars.name: Pliny the Younger
scholars.line: Roman governor of Bithynia whose letter to the emperor Trajan describes how early Christians worshipped.
works: Letter to Trajan on the Christians

scholars.name: Origen of Alexandria
scholars.line: Teacher in Alexandria and Caesarea who set the Hebrew Old Testament beside its Greek versions in six columns.
works: The Hexapla

scholars.name: Eusebius of Caesarea
scholars.line: Bishop of Caesarea and the first historian of the church; much of what we know of the early church comes through him.
works: Church History

scholars.name: Jerome
scholars.line: Learned Hebrew to translate the Bible into Latin; his Vulgate was the Bible of the Western church for a thousand years.
works: The Vulgate

scholars.name: Augustine of Hippo
scholars.line: Bishop of Hippo in North Africa; his thought shaped both Catholic and Protestant theology.
works: Confessions
The City of God

scholars.name: Anselm of Canterbury
scholars.line: Monk and archbishop of Canterbury who asked why God became man.
works: Why God Became Man

scholars.name: Thomas Aquinas
scholars.line: Dominican friar and teacher at Paris; the greatest of the medieval scholars, or 'schoolmen'.
works: Summa Theologiae

scholars.name: Desiderius Erasmus
scholars.line: Dutch scholar who printed the first published Greek New Testament, the text behind Luther's and Tyndale's translations.
works: Greek New Testament

scholars.name: William Tyndale
scholars.line: Translated the New Testament into English from the Greek, and was executed for it; much of his wording lives on in the King James Version.
works: English New Testament

scholars.name: James Ussher
scholars.line: Archbishop of Armagh and scholar who worked out a chronology of the world from Scripture and ancient histories.
works: Annals of the World

scholars.name: William Whiston
scholars.line: Cambridge mathematician whose English translation of Josephus is still the most reprinted one.
works: The Works of Josephus (translation)
site: His translation of Josephus is the edition in the library.

scholars.name: Edward Robinson
scholars.line: American scholar who travelled Palestine in 1838 and identified many biblical places; called the father of biblical geography.
works: Biblical Researches in Palestine
Later Biblical Researches in Palestine

scholars.name: William Smith
scholars.line: English lexicographer who edited the great Victorian Dictionary of the Bible.
works: Dictionary of the Bible
site: His dictionary is in the library, planned as a second dictionary voice.

scholars.name: Constantin von Tischendorf
scholars.line: German scholar who found Codex Sinaiticus, the oldest complete New Testament, at St Catherine's Monastery in Sinai.
works: Codex Sinaiticus published

scholars.name: Roswell D. Hitchcock
scholars.line: Professor at Union Seminary, New York, whose dictionary gives the meaning of nearly every name in the Bible.
works: Bible Names Dictionary
site: His names dictionary is in the library, planned for the meaning of names on people pages.

scholars.name: Philip Schaff
scholars.line: Swiss-born church historian in America; wrote an eight-volume history of the church and edited the Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers in English.
works: History of the Christian Church

scholars.name: A. R. Fausset
scholars.line: Anglican clergyman, co-author of the Jamieson-Fausset-Brown commentary and of a Bible encyclopaedia.
works: Bible Encyclopaedia and Dictionary
site: His encyclopaedia is in the library, planned as a dictionary voice.

scholars.name: James Strong
scholars.line: Methodist professor whose concordance gave every Hebrew and Greek word of the Bible a number, still used everywhere.
works: Exhaustive Concordance of the Bible
site: His word numbers are used in the Letters study.

scholars.name: M. G. Easton
scholars.line: Scottish minister whose Illustrated Bible Dictionary explains people, places and things of the Bible.
works: Illustrated Bible Dictionary
site: His articles appear on the Topics pages and in the study tables.

scholars.name: Alfred Edersheim
scholars.line: Vienna-born Jewish convert to Christ who described the Jewish world of the Gospels.
works: The Life and Times of Jesus the Messiah

scholars.name: B. F. Westcott
scholars.line: Cambridge professor and bishop of Durham; with Hort he edited a landmark Greek New Testament.
works: The New Testament in the Original Greek (with Hort)

scholars.name: Joseph Henry Thayer
scholars.line: Harvard professor whose Greek-English lexicon of the New Testament was the standard for decades.
works: Greek-English Lexicon of the New Testament
site: His lexicon is in the library, planned for Greek word meanings.

scholars.name: J. B. Lightfoot
scholars.line: Cambridge scholar and bishop of Durham; his commentaries on Paul's letters and his edition of the Apostolic Fathers are classics.
works: Commentary on Galatians
The Apostolic Fathers

scholars.name: F. J. A. Hort
scholars.line: Cambridge scholar who worked with Westcott for 28 years on the Greek text of the New Testament.
works: The New Testament in the Original Greek (with Westcott)

scholars.name: Orville J. Nave
scholars.line: United States Army chaplain who spent fourteen years gathering the Bible's verses by subject.
works: Nave's Topical Bible
site: One of the two books behind the site's Topics.

scholars.name: James Orr
scholars.line: Scottish theologian who edited the International Standard Bible Encyclopedia.
works: International Standard Bible Encyclopedia
site: His encyclopedia is in the library, planned as a reference voice.

scholars.name: S. R. Driver
scholars.line: Oxford Hebrew professor; with Francis Brown and Charles Briggs he made the standard Hebrew lexicon of the Old Testament.
works: Hebrew and English Lexicon (with Brown and Briggs)
site: The lexicon is in the library, planned for Hebrew word meanings.

scholars.name: William M. Ramsay
scholars.line: Scottish archaeologist who spent years in Asia Minor and found Luke a careful historian of Paul's journeys.
works: St. Paul the Traveller and the Roman Citizen
The Church in the Roman Empire Before A.D. 170

scholars.name: R. A. Torrey
scholars.line: Evangelist and Bible teacher whose New Topical Text Book gathers the Bible's verses under more than 600 subjects.
works: The New Topical Text Book
site: One of the two books behind the site's Topics, and a source for the miracles study.

scholars.name: A. T. Robertson
scholars.line: Greek scholar at Southern Baptist Seminary; his harmony sets the four Gospels side by side.
works: A Harmony of the Gospels
site: His harmony is the backbone of the site's Gospel harmony (185 events) and the miracles study.

scholars.name: William F. Albright
scholars.line: Johns Hopkins professor and the leading figure of 20th-century biblical archaeology.
works: The Archaeology of Palestine
From the Stone Age to Christianity

scholars.name: Kathleen Kenyon
scholars.line: British archaeologist who excavated Jericho and Jerusalem and refined how digs are recorded layer by layer.
works: Digging Up Jericho
Archaeology in the Holy Land

scholars.name: Yigael Yadin
scholars.line: Israeli archaeologist who excavated Hazor and Masada and published several of the Dead Sea Scrolls.
works: Masada
Hazor: The Rediscovery of a Great Citadel of the Bible

scholars.name: Charles Warren
scholars.line: Surveyed and explored Jerusalem's walls, tunnels, and ancient waterworks for the Palestine Exploration Fund.
works: The Recovery of Jerusalem
Underground Jerusalem

scholars.name: Flinders Petrie
scholars.line: Excavated Tell el-Hesi and helped establish pottery sequence and stratigraphic dating in Palestinian archaeology.
works: Tell el Hesy (Lachish)
Methods and Aims in Archaeology

scholars.name: Frederick Jones Bliss
scholars.line: Excavated Tell el-Hesi, Jerusalem, and sites in the southern Shephelah for the Palestine Exploration Fund.
works: A Mound of Many Cities: Tell el Hesy
Excavations in Palestine During the Years 1898–1900

scholars.name: John Garstang
scholars.line: Led major excavations at Jericho; his chronology and conclusions became a focus of later archaeological reassessment.
works: The Foundations of Bible History: Joshua, Judges
The Story of Jericho

scholars.name: Nelson Glueck
scholars.line: Rabbi and archaeologist whose surveys of Transjordan and the Negev mapped ancient settlements and trade routes.
works: The Other Side of the Jordan
Rivers in the Desert: A History of the Negev

scholars.name: Roland de Vaux
scholars.line: Directed excavations at Qumran and developed an influential, still debated interpretation of the settlement and Dead Sea Scrolls.
works: Ancient Israel: Its Life and Institutions
Archaeology and the Dead Sea Scrolls

scholars.name: Olga Tufnell
scholars.line: Worked on the Lachish excavations and brought their Iron and Bronze Age finds into the final excavation reports.
works: Lachish III: The Iron Age
Lachish IV: The Bronze Age

scholars.name: G. Ernest Wright
scholars.line: Archaeologist and biblical scholar who directed excavations at Shechem and wrote widely on archaeology and Israelite history.
works: Biblical Archaeology
Shechem: The Biography of a Biblical City

scholars.name: Avraham Biran
scholars.line: Directed the long-running Tel Dan excavations, including the discovery of the inscription mentioning the House of David.
works: Biblical Dan
Dan I: A Chronicle of the Excavations, the Pottery Neolithic, the Early Bronze Age and the Middle Bronze Age Tombs

scholars.name: Amihai Mazar
scholars.line: Archaeologist of ancient Israel whose excavations and synthesis examine settlement, chronology, and material culture.
works: Archaeology of the Land of the Bible: 10,000–586 B.C.E.
Timnah: A Biblical Town in the Sorek Valley

scholars.name: Lawrence E. Stager
scholars.line: Directed the Leon Levy Expedition to Ashkelon, documenting the city's long history through excavation reports.
works: Ashkelon 1: Introduction and Overview (1985–2006)
Ashkelon 3: The Seventh Century B.C.

scholars.name: Israel Finkelstein
scholars.line: Archaeologist of the Levant whose surveys and contested chronological proposals have reshaped debate about ancient Israel.
works: The Archaeology of the Israelite Settlement
The Bible Unearthed

scholars.name: Jodi Magness
scholars.line: Archaeologist of the Second Temple and early Roman periods whose work examines Qumran and the wider Holy Land.
works: The Archaeology of Qumran and the Dead Sea Scrolls
The Archaeology of the Holy Land

scholars.name: Austen Henry Layard
scholars.line: Excavated the Assyrian palaces at Nimrud and Nineveh, publishing reliefs, inscriptions, and accounts of the fieldwork.
works: Nineveh and Its Remains
Discoveries in the Ruins of Nineveh and Babylon

scholars.name: Hormuzd Rassam
scholars.line: Mosul-born archaeologist who excavated at Nineveh, Nimrud, Babylon, and Sippar and recovered major collections of cuneiform tablets.
works: Asshur and the Land of Nimrod

scholars.name: George Smith (Assyriologist)
scholars.line: Assyriologist and excavator who identified the Babylonian flood narrative among tablets from Nineveh and published Mesopotamian texts and discoveries.
works: Assyrian Discoveries
The Chaldean Account of Genesis

scholars.name: Robert Koldewey
scholars.line: Directed the German excavations at Babylon, documenting its temples, palaces, fortifications, and the Ishtar Gate.
works: The Excavations at Babylon

scholars.name: James Henry Breasted
scholars.line: Egyptologist whose epigraphic surveys and translations made Egyptian historical inscriptions widely available for studying the ancient Near East.
works: A History of Egypt
Ancient Records of Egypt
Development of Religion and Thought in Ancient Egypt

scholars.name: Leonard Woolley
scholars.line: Directed the excavations at Ur, documenting the Royal Cemetery, the ziggurat, houses, and the development of ancient Mesopotamian urban life.
works: Ur Excavations II: The Royal Cemetery
Ur Excavations V: The Ziggurat and Its Surroundings
Excavations at Ur: A Record of Twelve Years' Work

scholars.name: Nahman Avigad
scholars.line: Excavated Jerusalem's Jewish Quarter and studied ancient Hebrew inscriptions, seals, and the material culture of the city.
works: Discovering Jerusalem
Corpus of West Semitic Stamp Seals

scholars.name: Benjamin Mazar
scholars.line: Combined historical geography with excavation at Tell Qasile, Beth Shearim, and the area south and west of Jerusalem's Temple Mount.
works: The Mountain of the Lord
The Early Biblical Period: Historical Essays

scholars.name: Kurt Bittel
scholars.line: Directed excavations at the Hittite capital Hattusha, documenting its architecture and material culture within the wider ancient Near East.
works: Hattusha: The Capital of the Hittites
Les Hittites

scholars.name: James B. Pritchard
scholars.line: Excavated Gibeon, Tell es-Sa'idiyeh, and Sarepta and edited ancient Near Eastern texts used to study the Bible's historical setting.
works: Ancient Near Eastern Texts Relating to the Old Testament
Gibeon, Where the Sun Stood Still
Recovering Sarepta, a Phoenician City

scholars.name: Trude Dothan
scholars.line: Specialist in Philistine material culture who excavated Deir el-Balah and co-directed the Tel Miqne-Ekron project.
works: The Philistines and Their Material Culture
People of the Sea: The Search for the Philistines

scholars.name: William G. Dever
scholars.line: Excavator of Gezer and interpreter of ancient Israel whose work examines settlement, daily life, religion, and the relationship between archaeology and biblical texts.
works: What Did the Biblical Writers Know and When Did They Know It?
Who Were the Early Israelites and Where Did They Come From?
The Lives of Ordinary People in Ancient Israel
Beyond the Texts: An Archaeological Portrait of Ancient Israel and Judah
My Nine Lives: Sixty Years in Israeli and Biblical Archaeology
scholars.match: William G\. Dever|William Dever|William Gwinn Dever

scholars.name: Ehud Netzer
scholars.line: Archaeologist and architect who excavated Herodian palaces at Jericho, Masada, and Herodium and studied their construction and development.
works: Masada III: The Buildings, Stratigraphy and Architecture
Hasmonean and Herodian Palaces at Jericho I: Stratigraphy and Architecture
The Architecture of Herod, the Great Builder

scholars.name: David Ussishkin
scholars.line: Directed renewed excavations at Lachish and investigated its destruction levels, siege works, and relationship to Assyrian records.
works: The Conquest of Lachish by Sennacherib
Biblical Lachish: A Tale of Construction, Destruction, Excavation and Restoration

scholars.name: Amnon Ben-Tor
scholars.line: Led the renewed Hazor excavations and edited reports on its Canaanite and Israelite remains, as well as a broad survey of Israel's archaeology.
works: The Archaeology of Ancient Israel
Hazor VI: The 1990–2009 Excavations, the Iron Age
Hazor: Canaanite Metropolis, Israelite City

scholars.name: Seymour Gitin
scholars.line: Co-directed the Tel Miqne-Ekron excavations and published research on Philistine industry, the Ekron inscription, and ceramic chronology.
works: A Royal Dedicatory Inscription from Ekron
The Ancient Pottery of Israel and Its Neighbors, Volumes 1–2
The Ancient Pottery of Israel and Its Neighbors, Volume 3

scholars.name: Yigal Shiloh
scholars.line: Directed the City of David excavations and studied Israelite masonry, architecture, and the development of ancient Jerusalem.
works: The Proto-Aeolic Capital and Israelite Ashlar Masonry
Excavations at the City of David I

scholars.name: Carol L. Meyers
scholars.line: Archaeologist of ancient Israel whose research combines household remains, social history, and biblical texts to study everyday life and women's activities.
works: Discovering Eve: Ancient Israelite Women in Context
Household Archaeology in Ancient Israel and Beyond

scholars.name: Ronny Reich
scholars.line: Excavated ancient Jerusalem with Eli Shukron and studied its water systems, the City of David, and Jewish ritual baths.
works: Excavating the City of David: Where Jerusalem's History Began
The Date of the Siloam Tunnel Reconsidered

scholars.name: Thomas E. Levy
scholars.line: Field archaeologist whose projects in Israel and Jordan combine excavation, radiocarbon dating, and metallurgy to study ancient societies and Edomite copper production.
works: Historical Biblical Archaeology and the Future: The New Pragmatism
New Insights into the Iron Age Archaeology of Edom, Southern Jordan

scholars.name: Eilat Mazar
scholars.line: Directed excavations at the Ophel and City of David, publishing architectural remains, pottery, and seal impressions; some proposed building identifications remain debated.
works: The Ophel Excavations to the South of the Temple Mount 2009–2013: Final Reports, Volume I
The Ophel Excavations to the South of the Temple Mount 2009–2013: Final Reports, Volume II

scholars.name: Yosef Garfinkel
scholars.line: Excavator of Khirbet Qeiyafa and Lachish whose reports and interpretations contribute to debate about the emergence of the kingdom of Judah.
works: Khirbet Qeiyafa I: Excavation Report 2007–2008
In the Footsteps of King David: Revelations from an Ancient Biblical City

scholars.name: Aren M. Maeir
scholars.line: Directs the Tell es-Safi/Gath project, investigating Philistine culture, urban life, trade, and scientific methods of dating excavated contexts.
works: Tell es-Safi/Gath I: The 1996–2005 Seasons
Characterization of Contexts for Radiocarbon Dating: Results from the Early Iron Age at Tell es-Safi/Gath, Israel

scholars.name: Eric H. Cline
scholars.line: Excavator at Megiddo and Tel Kabri whose books examine Bronze Age societies, archaeological methods, and the history of biblical archaeology.
works: Biblical Archaeology: A Very Short Introduction
1177 B.C.: The Year Civilization Collapsed
Three Stones Make a Wall: The Story of Archaeology
Digging Up Armageddon: The Search for the Lost City of Solomon
After 1177 B.C.: The Survival of Civilizations

scholars.name: William Lane Craig
scholars.line: Christian philosopher, theologian and debater whose apologetics writings examine the existence of God, the resurrection of Jesus, and faith and reason.
works: The Kalam Cosmological Argument
Reasonable Faith, third edition
site: 177 Reasonable Faith PDFs held locally with page-by-page text extraction. Browse the catalogue for original articles and PDFs.

finds.name: Robinson's Arch
finds.line: The spring of a great arch on the Temple Mount's western wall, recognised by Edward Robinson.

finds.name: Codex Sinaiticus
finds.line: A complete New Testament from the 300s, found at the monastery by Tischendorf (first leaves in 1844, the codex in 1859).

finds.name: Paul's roads in Asia Minor
finds.line: Ramsay's years of travel through the towns of Paul's journeys, from the 1880s.

finds.name: Dead Sea Scrolls
finds.line: Scrolls found by shepherds in caves near Qumran, with the oldest known copies of Old Testament books; Yadin later published several.

finds.name: Hazor
finds.line: Yadin's excavations of the great Canaanite city, 1955 to 1958.

finds.name: Masada
finds.line: Yadin's excavation of Herod's fortress, 1963 to 1965.

chain.about: How the Bible's text reached English readers, through these scholars' hands.
steps: Set the Hebrew beside its Greek versions
Translated it into Latin from the Hebrew
Translated it into English from the Greek
Found one of the oldest complete New Testaments
Edited the Greek text anew, with Hort
Edited the Greek text anew, with Westcott
